description: Lists the pods of a Kubernetes namespace with status, restarts and age, shows and follows a container's logs, and restarts a pod after you confirm. It runs kubectl on this device with your own kubeconfig: your cluster credentials never leave this device and are never sent to the RIM server or to the AI model provider. Pod logs reach the AI agent only if you allow its Pods: Show logs command in the plugin's AI access settings.
author: RIM team

commands.title: Pods: Refresh
commands.description: Lists the pods of the chosen kubeconfig context and namespace again.

commands.title: Pods: Filter
commands.description: Chooses the context, namespace, name filter or refresh interval, then lists the pods. Without arguments it clears the name filter.

arguments.name: text
arguments.description: Show only pods whose name or status contains this text. Empty clears it.

arguments.name: interval_seconds
arguments.description: Refresh every this many seconds, 5 to 3600, or 0 to stop.

commands.title: Pods: Restart pod
commands.description: Deletes a pod so its controller starts a fresh one. Asks you to confirm first; the AI agent can suggest it but never run it.

arguments.name: namespace
arguments.description: Defaults to the namespace the panel shows.

arguments.name: context
arguments.description: Defaults to the context the panel shows.

commands.title: Pods: Show logs
commands.description: Shows the last lines a pod's container printed, and follows new ones in the Pods panel. The AI agent may read them only if you allow this command in the plugin's AI access settings; it never follows them.

arguments.name: container
arguments.description: Container to read. Defaults to the pod's default container, as kubectl picks it.

arguments.name: tail_lines
arguments.description: How many of the last lines to show, 1 to 5000. Defaults to the last count chosen, at first the Log lines setting (100 unless changed).

arguments.name: previous
arguments.description: Read the container's previous run, e.g. after a crash.

arguments.name: follow
arguments.description: Keep adding new lines as the container prints them, in the Pods panel.

arguments.name: namespace
arguments.description: Defaults to the namespace the panel shows.

arguments.name: context
arguments.description: Defaults to the context the panel shows.

commands.title: Pods: Stop following logs
commands.description: Stops following a pod's logs in the Pods panel; with close, closes the log view too.

arguments.name: close
arguments.description: Close the log view as well.

panels.title: Pods
panels.description: Pods of one namespace, refreshed on an interval, and a container's logs.

settings_schema.title: Kubeconfig file
settings_schema.description: The kubeconfig kubectl reads, passed to it as --kubeconfig. ~ stands for your home folder. Empty uses $KUBECONFIG, or ~/.kube/config.

settings_schema.title: kubectl path
settings_schema.description: The kubectl program to run: a full path, or a name on your PATH. Empty uses $RIM_KUBECTL when set, else the kubectl on your PATH or in a usual install folder.

settings_schema.title: Default context
settings_schema.description: The kubeconfig context the Pods panel opens on, until you pick another. Empty uses the kubeconfig's current context.

settings_schema.title: Default namespace
settings_schema.description: The namespace the Pods panel shows in every context until you pick another. Empty uses the context's namespace from the kubeconfig, else default.

settings_schema.title: Refresh every (seconds)
settings_schema.description: How often the Pods panel lists the pods again, 5 to 3600 seconds. Turn refreshing off in the panel.

settings_schema.title: Log lines
settings_schema.description: How many of a container's last lines a log view starts with, 1 to 5000, until you pick another count in the view.
